abstract_sentences.text: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have advanced graph classification, yet they remain vulnerable to graph-level imbalance, encompassing class imbalance and topological imbalance.

evidence.anchor: remain vulnerable to graph-level imbalance, encompassing class imbalance and topological imbalance

abstract_sentences.text: To address both types of imbalance in a unified manner, we propose UniImb, a Unified framework for Imbalanced graph classification.

evidence.anchor: we propose UniImb, a Unified framework

abstract_sentences.text: Specifically, UniImb first captures multi-scale topological features and enhances data diversity via learnable personalized graph perturbations.

evidence.anchor: captures multi-scale topological features ... learnable personalized graph perturbations

abstract_sentences.text: It then employs a dynamic balanced prototype module to learn representative prototypes from graph instances, improving the quality of graph representations.

evidence.anchor: dynamic balanced prototype module to learn representative prototypes

abstract_sentences.text: Concurrently, a prototype load-balancing optimization term mitigates dominance by majority samples to equalize sample influence during training.

evidence.anchor: load-balancing optimization term mitigates dominance by majority samples

abstract_sentences.text: We justify these design choices theoretically using the Information Bottleneck principle.

evidence.anchor: justify these design choices theoretically using the Information Bottleneck principle

abstract_sentences.text: Extensive experiments on 19 datasets-including a large-scale imbalanced air pollution graph dataset AirGraph released by us and 23 baselines demonstrate that UniImb has achieved dominant performance across various imbalanced scenarios.

evidence.anchor: 19 datasets ... AirGraph ... 23 baselines ... dominant performance

abstract_sentences.text: Our code is available at GitHub.

evidence.anchor: Our code is available at GitHub

introduction_moves.move: context → problem：以 GNN neighborhood aggregation 与 graph classification 建立对象，随后指出现有架构依赖 balanced graph datasets，并定义 class/topological 两类 graph-level imbalance。

evidence.anchor: graph data often exhibits imbalanced distributions

introduction_moves.move: failure_of_prior_work：分别回顾 class-imbalance 的 graph-of-graphs/G2GNN/ImGKB 与 topology-imbalance 的 reweighting/augmentation/SOLT-GNN/TopoImb，说明各自只覆盖单一偏斜。

evidence.anchor: focus unilaterally on either class imbalance or topological imbalance

introduction_moves.move: missing_insight → core_idea：把复杂、交织的 class/topology imbalance 缺口收束为 balanced extraction，用 shared prototype features 同时补充 minority-class 与 small-scale tail graphs。

evidence.anchor: extract semantically shared prototype features via a balanced extraction

introduction_moves.move: method_preview → theory_preview → contribution_list：预览 topology encoding、graph-dependent perturbation、local-prior GNN、DBP、Uniform activation 与 tail enhancement，之后列出四项贡献和 19 datasets/AirGraph/3D/backbone 范围。

evidence.anchor: Contributions ... Unified Insight ... Empirical Study

evidence.anchor: restricted random walk kernel with the global graph information bottleneck

evidence.anchor: The development of a unified imbalanced graph learning framework remains an unexplored challenge

evidence.anchor: Early work ... focused on spectral methods ... and random walks

evidence.anchor: cannot be directly transferred to this scenario

related_work_moves.move: positioning_only → gap_creation：Appendix B.3 扩展 edge-level imbalance；B.4 指出关键 molecular subgraph 稀少却重要，subgraph imbalance 仍少有处理。

evidence.anchor: the issue of subgraph imbalance remains largely unaddressed

method_moves.move: setup_notation：定义 G={V,E,A,X}、N 个 graph instances、labels Y 和 graph-level mapping F。

evidence.anchor: the goal of the graph-level classification task

method_moves.move: state_problem：以 Figure 1 将输入 imbalance、topology/perturbation、GNN 与 DBP 串成 tail graph representation pipeline。

evidence.anchor: enhancing the model’s capability to represent tail graphs

method_moves.move: define_component：Local Topology Encoding 用 M=D^{-1}A 和 z-step self-landing probability 形成 LE。

evidence.anchor: only the landing probability of the node vj to itself

method_moves.move: define_component：Global Topology Encoding 对 Laplacian 求前 z 个 eigenvalues/eigenvectors，经 permutation-invariant φ/ℓ 形成 GE。

evidence.anchor: global structural properties, such as subgraph frequency and connectivity

method_moves.move: explain_mechanism：Edge Drop 以 average degree 经 MLP/sigmoid 学习 graph-specific Bernoulli probability，并作用于 adjacency。

evidence.anchor: customizes learnable perturbations based on the unique characteristics of each graph

method_moves.move: explain_mechanism：Feature Mask 用 node-level Bernoulli mask 作用于 node features，形成第二种 personalized perturbation。

evidence.anchor: personalized feature mask distribution

method_moves.move: instantiate_algorithm：将初始 feature、GE、LE 送入 GIN；Eq. (3) 更新 graph feature，Eq. (4) 用独立 GNN 更新 local encoding。

evidence.anchor: independent GNN layer to update the local topology encoding

method_moves.move: derive → connect_to_prediction：READOUT 由 Eq. (5) 生成 H，随后 Feature Mixup 产生 2N 行表示，插值细节在 Appendix C。

evidence.anchor: a Feature Mixup strategy ... generating a new matrix

method_moves.move: define_component：DBP 定义 K 个 learnable prototype embeddings S，要求 K≪N。

evidence.anchor: prototypes are defined as a set of learnable embeddings

method_moves.move: derive：Prototype Perception 以 TopK1 从 graph-prototype similarity 选择 graph 并聚合为 H~S。

evidence.anchor: Prototypes are perceived from the graph data based on the attention coefficients

method_moves.move: derive：Prototype Balance 以 TopK2 选择每个 graph 的相关 prototype，加 γ 和 Sigmoid 得到 H^b。

evidence.anchor: selecting the most relevant prototype to enhance its representational capacity

method_moves.move: state_problem：指出 imbalanced distribution 可能使 prototype 偏向 head data，转入 Information Bottleneck。

evidence.anchor: these learned prototypes may become biased due to imbalanced graph data distributions

method_moves.move: derive → theory：Theory 1 以 min I(S;G)-βI(S;Y) 把 label relevance 与 input redundancy 分开。

evidence.anchor: reducing the redundancy of imbalanced input information

method_moves.move: derive → connect_to_prediction：Proposition 1 将 mutual information 转成 KL(P||U)，附录用 auxiliary marginal、empirical distribution 与 Taylor expansion 补全推导。

evidence.anchor: min KL(P||U)

method_moves.move: derive → instantiate_algorithm：Proposition 2 定义 prototype hit count、η modulation、StopGrad surrogate 和 sign update。

evidence.anchor: TopK operation is non-differentiable in practice

method_moves.move: contrast_alternative：比较 Uniform、Zipf、Exponential、Poisson 四种 U，并用 Table 1/Appendix D.4 选择 Uniform。

evidence.anchor: when the empirical distribution U follows a uniform distribution

method_moves.move: connect_to_experiment：取 H^b 前 N 行送入两层 MLP decoder；Algorithm 1 分别更新 Θ 与 η。

evidence.anchor: the first N rows of H^b

experimental_design.name: dataset_scope
experimental_design.description: 19 datasets are claimed, comprising 12 common graph datasets, AirGraph, three MoleculeNet 3D datasets, and Enzymes/Letter-high/Letter-low multi-class additions.

evidence.anchor: 19 datasets ... AirGraph ... 23 baselines
12 widely-adopted graph datasets
Enzymes ... Letter-high ... Letter-low

experimental_design.name: common_datasets
experimental_design.description: MUTAG, PTC-MR, PROTEINS, D&D, NCI1, DHFR, AIDS, FRANKENSTEIN, REDDIT-B, COLLAB, Synthie and IMDB-MULTI cover chemical, protein, social/collaboration and synthetic domains.

evidence.anchor: These datasets cover a range of domains

experimental_design.name: airgraph
experimental_design.description: AirGraph has 30,660 province-level graphs from 1,341 stations across 28 provinces, with past-24-hour node features and future-24-hour pollution labels; high pollution is 6.86%.

evidence.anchor: 30,660 graph instances ... high pollution category accounts for only 6.86%

experimental_design.name: 3d_datasets
experimental_design.description: BBBP, BACE and HIV are evaluated with SchNet, DimeNet and SphereNet; G2GNN/TopoImb/ImbGNN use SphereNet and UniImb retains only DBP.

evidence.anchor: For our model, we retain only the core DBP module

experimental_design.name: class_split
experimental_design.description: Binary class-imbalance data use 25% train, 25% validation and 50% test with extreme/medium/low ratios 9/2.33/1; multi-class uses 25%/10%/65% and ratios about 100/20/1.

evidence.anchor: split the dataset into 25% for training and 25% for validation
highly imbalanced setting ρ ≈100 ... moderately ... ρ ≈20

experimental_design.name: topology_split
experimental_design.description: Eight modified datasets use 10% train, 10% validation and 80% test, class-balanced splits, head as top 20% largest graphs and tail as remaining 80%; realized ratios are approximate.

evidence.anchor: top 20% of graphs with the largest number of nodes
challenging to strictly satisfy the target sparsity ratio

experimental_design.name: intertwined_split
experimental_design.description: Six datasets combine class and topology skew with 10%/10%/80% splitting; binary class ratio is 1/9 and each class has 10% topology-head versus 90% tail graphs.

evidence.anchor: class-imbalance and topological-imbalance are interwoven
class & topology

experimental_design.name: baseline_scope
experimental_design.description: The main text enumerates five baseline groups and 23 representative baselines spanning classic GNN, graph transformer, 3D, class-imbalance and topology-imbalance methods.

evidence.anchor: four categories of baselines ... ❺ Topology-imbalance Methods

experimental_design.name: training
experimental_design.description: Implementation uses PyTorch on a 40GB NVIDIA A100, Adam with learning rate 0.001, five GNN layers, φ=0.001, and 20 repeated runs reporting average and standard deviation.

evidence.anchor: 40GB NVIDIA A100 GPU ... All experiments are repeated 20 times

experimental_design.name: features
experimental_design.description: REDDIT-B, IMDB-MULTI and COLLAB use one-hot node-degree features; other dataset feature details are in Table 8 and Appendix G.

evidence.anchor: one-hot encodings of node degrees as node features

final_judgment.single_storyline: Class imbalance and graph-size topological imbalance are framed as tail graph contribution deficits. Multi-scale topology encoding and personalized perturbation enrich inputs; DBP perception/balance plus Uniform-prior load regulation redistribute prototype interactions before classification. [p.2-p.6, Sections 1 and 4, interpretation]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the two imbalance definitions, Figure 1 pipeline, Eq. (1)-(12), Information Bottleneck objective, Uniform choice, 20-run protocol, extreme Tables 2-5 and Figures 4-6, plus the 19-dataset/23-baseline scope. [p.1-p.10, explicit]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Feature Mixup, KL/Taylor proofs, Algorithm 1, ratio definitions, dataset construction, hyperparameters, metric formulas, low/medium/full results, TopK/backbone/DBP-only tests and limitations are moved to p.17-p.38. [p.17-p.38, explicit]
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 makes the DBP dataflow and TopK selection concrete; Tables 2-3 align baseline columns; Table 5 tests a 3D domain; Figure 6 supplies a representation diagnostic. [p.3, p.7-p.10, interpretation]
final_judgment.largest_gap: Information Bottleneck supports an MI/KL objective and η surrogate, but no convergence, tail-influence or classification-performance guarantee is established. AirGraph efficiency also relies on a single bubble figure without a complete numeric table. [p.5-p.6, p.9, p.20-p.24, interpretation]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a unified imbalance claim, define a shared state variable and an observable contribution/load quantity, then pair component deletion with results stratified by the original imbalance axes. [p.3-p.10, p.31-p.38, interpretation]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule applies to graph-level imbalance where head/tail graph units and a representation interface are explicit. It does not establish transfer to heterogeneous graphs, few-shot/dynamic/anomaly tasks or convergence/generalization guarantees. [p.38, Appendix J, explicit]

reading_notes.physical_reading: All 38 physical PDF pages and all 43 extracted text form-feed segments were read, including p.11-p.16 references, Appendix A-J, all visible Figures 1-16, Tables 1-24 and Algorithm 1.
reading_notes.layout: Two-column proceedings layout. Figure 1 is a wide architecture figure; p.9 combines Table 4, Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 4 and the beginning of Figure 5; p.32-p.38 are table/figure-heavy appendix pages.
reading_notes.statistical_boundary: Visible statistical summaries are 20-run mean ± standard deviation and selected Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test p<0.05 stars. No multiple-comparison correction, bootstrap, Bayesian analysis, regression or conventional confidence intervals are reported.
reading_notes.ablation_boundary: A named component-ablation section is present in Section 5.5; Appendix I adds Micro-F1, static perturbation, TopK, imbalance-degree, backbone and DBP-only checks.
reading_notes.lexical_notes: Core terms are graph, imbalance, class, topological, dataset, performance, prototype, representation, learning, distribution, Information Bottleneck, TopK1 and TopK2. Macro-F1/Micro-F1, Greek symbols, G2GNN and NULL-separated chart text are error-prone for automatic token counts.
